excluded_claims: A claim that any software vendor, platform, or AI tool is required by the cited regulators or professional bodies.
A claim that digital architecture is a standalone BLEA subject.
A claim that AI outputs, code-compliance automation, or generative design can replace professional judgment.
General encyclopedia, news, blog, or commercial rendering articles as primary authority.

proposed.text: An architect uses BIM to coordinate a complex multi-disciplinary project, detects clashes, and resolves them in the model before construction. A different architect uses traditional drawings and manages coordination in the field during construction. What does this scenario illustrate about digital tools and professional practice?

options.text: The outcome depends on the architect's skill, not the tools used; both methods are equally rigorous in theory
Both approaches achieve the same result; digital tools are merely convenient but not essential for successful project delivery
The first approach prevents costly field modifications and rework, demonstrating how digital coordination tools improve efficiency and cost; the second approach accepts wasteful field problem-solving
Field coordination is more authentic and reflects traditional craftsmanship; digital approaches sacrifice this value for efficiency

rationale.a: While skill matters, tools enable or constrain capability; digital coordination is objectively superior when available.
rationale.b: While outcomes might be similar, the second approach is wasteful; efficiency matters.
rationale.d: Craftsmanship includes efficient problem-solving; field coordination is less elegant than thoughtful preconstruction planning.
rationale.correct: The scenario illustrates the value of model-based coordination when it prevents field conflicts and rework. The source-safe claim is efficiency and coordination support, not that BIM is always legally required.
rationale.takeaway: Digital coordination can reduce waste when properly used.
rationale.source_boundary: Batch 159 supports digital architecture as technological-trend and professional-practice evidence, not as a vendor mandate or standalone BLEA subject.
